cases.excerpt: Among 49,472 men, 4134 were diagnosed with prostate cancer during an average follow-up period of 11.2 years.

comparison.excerpt: comparing the highest with lowest quartile

confidence_interval.excerpt: Consumption of total, individual, or subgroups of dairy products was not statistically significantly associated with prostate cancer risk overall (HR = 1.05, 95% CI = 0.96-1.15 comparing the highest with lowest quartile) or stratified by severity, except for regular-fat dairy product intake with late-stage prostate cancer risk (HR = 1.37, 95% CI = 1.04-1.82 comparing the highest with lowest quartile) and 2%-fat milk intake with advanced prostate cancer risk (HR = 1.14, 95% CI = 1.02-1.28 comparing the higher than median intake with no intake group).

continent.excerpt: among men in the United States

design.excerpt: We prospectively investigated the associations between dairy product consumption and prostate cancer risk among men in the United States.

effect_size.excerpt: Consumption of total, individual, or subgroups of dairy products was not statistically significantly associated with prostate cancer risk overall (HR = 1.05, 95% CI = 0.96-1.15 comparing the highest with lowest quartile) or stratified by severity, except for regular-fat dairy product intake with late-stage prostate cancer risk (HR = 1.37, 95% CI = 1.04-1.82 comparing the highest with lowest quartile) and 2%-fat milk intake with advanced prostate cancer risk (HR = 1.14, 95% CI = 1.02-1.28 comparing the higher than median intake with no intake group).

exposure_measurement.excerpt: using a validated food frequency questionnaire

sample_size.excerpt: After calculating pre-diagnostic intake of individual or subgroups of dairy products using a validated food frequency questionnaire, we estimated hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for pathologically-verified cases of incident prostate cancer among men, overall, or stratified by severity. Among 49,472 men, 4134 were diagnosed with prostate cancer during an average follow-up period of 11.2 years.

evidence_scope_projection.definition: Overall prostate cancer evidence, excluding estimates solely about aggressive prostate cancer. General estimates from papers that also report aggressive endpoints remain included. Uncertain endpoints retain their existing review and pooling restrictions.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test does not indicate significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.1182) for the meta-analysis of Dairy and Prostate cancer\aggressive. There is no statistical evidence of small-study effects based on this test, although the absence of significance does not rule out publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 23 studies yielded an overall effect size of 1.22 (95% CI: 1.11–1.34), suggesting that dairy is associated with a higher risk of prostate cancer\aggressive. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was very high between-study heterogeneity (I² = 83.30%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
